slides.title: Reversing the margin decline

paragraphs.text: Reversing the margin decline
Margin plan and first actions, for the board meeting of February 2027
Harlow Fresh Markets
CEO and board
Board discussion document; figures from the management briefing pack (synthetic data)

slides.title: Key questions

paragraphs.text: Key questions
How can Harlow lift its operating margin from 1.0% in FY2025 to at least 3.0% by FY2028, within $25M of one-time cost and the $20M FY2026 covenant, and which actions should come first?
Why did the operating margin fall from 3.4% to 1.0%, and how large is the gap to the target?
Is store labor the cause, and what should Harlow do with hours, shrink and its weakest stores?
How much margin do promotions cost, and how far can Harlow cut them without losing to ValuMart?
Does e-commerce make money, and how can it keep its customers while losing less?
Which moves reach 3.0% by FY2028, and which come first?
Decision maker
Success criteria
Timing
Out of scope
CEO, seeking board approval of the margin plan and its first actions

Operating margin of at least 3.0% by FY2028; Operating income of at least $20M in FY2026 (lender covenant); At most $25M of one-time cost or capital over FY2026–FY2028; No closure of a store with a lease beyond 2027 without a board vote; delivery kept in some form
Board meeting, February 2027
Closing delivery (owners' commitment); Refinancing the covenant; Spending beyond the $25M budget

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Fix promotions, shrink and delivery pricing, not hours: with store exits, the margin reaches 3.0% by FY2028
Promotions, shrink and e-commerce caused 87% of the margin fall; wages only 13%
–	Operating income fell 68% while sales grew 6%; the target needs $29.8M more a year
Move store hours instead of cutting them, and exit the nine loss-making stores
–	An 8% cut could lose $10.0M of its $14.5M saving to shrink; moving hours saves $4.2M
Return promotions to the FY2023 mix outside ValuMart areas, and grow private label
–	Promotion mix caused over two-thirds of the gross-margin fall; the reset adds $9.9M
Keep e-commerce but charge for delivery, which wins back $2.8M of a $10.4M loss
–	Each home delivery loses about $12; the fee test lost only 2% of e-commerce sales
First: promotions, delivery fees and store hours, which need no capital
–	Five moves add $27.4M a year and lift the margin to 3.0% by FY2028
–	Together the first three cover the FY2026 covenant need; $6.5M of reserves cover most wage risk
